This is one dissent recorded in a manifesto about sustaining human knowledge in the age of AI. Which fault line does it fall on?

Options:
- consent_or_payment: consent and payment mechanism: opt-in / levies / dues on existing text vs open training, pay at output, contracts for new work (Salib, Bratton, O'Reilly against the majority)
- model_in_loop: whether a model belongs in the checking loop or the room at all (Becker, Turkle)
- other: anything else

Text:

Designs assume good faith and usage markets reward seeding campaigns; identity registries endanger activists, and governance should center the reader's right to receive information.
raw: {"choice":"other","why":"The dissent objects that \"designs assume good faith\" and that \"usage markets reward seeding campaigns.\" It also warns that \"identity registries endanger activists\" and asks governance to \"center the reader's right to receive information.\" These points concern adversarial manipulation, privacy risks and readers' rights. They do not take a side on opt-in, levies or pay-at-output, and they say nothing about whether a model belongs in the checking loop."}

parsed.why: The dissent objects that "designs assume good faith" and that "usage markets reward seeding campaigns." It also warns that "identity registries endanger activists" and asks governance to "center the reader's right to receive information." These points concern adversarial manipulation, privacy risks and readers' rights. They do not take a side on opt-in, levies or pay-at-output, and they say nothing about whether a model belongs in the checking loop.
